method: llm_inference --dumpProfile --warmup 1, TRT-reported GPU time per stage; frames = robovqa_0_*.jpg at <=448px
note_plugin: EDGELLM_PLUGIN_PATH must be exported explicitly; ~/.bashrc returns early for non-interactive shells, and the relative fallback path only resolves when cwd is the TensorRT-Edge-LLM dir
repeatability: 6-frame vision encoder measured 144.52 ms and 146.17 ms on two runs (1.1% apart)

constraints.implication: 112 image tokens/frame => at most 8 frames (896 tokens) plus a short prompt fit; 9+ frames requires rebuilding the LLM engine with a larger maxInputLen

caveats.decode_number_unused: llm_inference reports 'Average Time per Token: ~16.3 ms' for generation, but that divides a single decode step's GPU time (32.93 ms) by 'Generated Tokens: 2' (which counts the prefill-produced first token). 32.93 ms matches llm_bench's 33.13 ms E2E TPOT, so TPOT is reported from llm_bench, not from this field.
caveats.peak_memory_scope: Peak unified memory is ~4856 MB regardless of frame count and ~equals the LLM engine size alone, so this counter appears to exclude the separately-loaded visual engine; reported verbatim, scope not confirmed.
caveats.int8_vision_blocked: visual_build exposes no precision flag (only onnxDir/engineDir/token limits) => the vision encoder's fp16 precision is fixed by the exported ONNX. Quantizing it requires re-exporting in the cloud (Kaggle), which needs the HF/Kaggle credentials pending rotation.

vision_encoder_config.source: engines/int4/visual/config.json on orin-dog (exported by TRTEdge visual_build)
vision_encoder_config.params_from_engine_size: 1167925844 B / 2 B per fp16 param = 583.96 M params
vision_encoder_config.params_analytic: 27 layers x (4*1152^2 + 2*1152*4304) = 411.1 M backbone; + patch embed 1.77 M + pos embed 2.65 M + merger + 3 deepstack mergers ~= 0.58 B total (agrees with the engine-derived 584 M to ~1.4%)

preprocessing.our_step: sample 6 frames uniformly per benchmark video, resize long side to 448 px keeping aspect ratio

actual_frame_sizes_measured.note: 1260 jpgs = 210 items x 6 frames, measured with PIL on orin-dog:~/bench/frames

preprocessing.processor: Qwen2VLImageProcessor (engines/int4/visual/preprocessor_config.json): do_convert_rgb, bicubic resize (resample=3) to a multiple of patch_size*merge_size = 32 with total pixels in [100352, 2097152], rescale 1/255, normalize mean=std=0.5

tokens_per_frame.rule: tokens = (W/32) x (H/32) after resize, because 2x2 spatial merge makes one token cover 32x32 px

runs_448x358_2026_07_26.reading: vision time scales with patch count: 616/448 = 1.375x patches -> 195.68/138.05 = 1.42x time (0.212 vs 0.205 ms per output token). The 448x252 prefill reproduces the earlier sweep (446.66 vs 446.41 ms); the vision number is 5.6% below the earlier 146.17 ms, i.e. session-to-session variance, so the two shapes are compared within this session only.

max_input_len_headroom_2026_07_26.finding: the worst-case request in the n=210 benchmark is 1015 tokens against the engine's maxInputLen=1024 -- 9 tokens of headroom
max_input_len_headroom_2026_07_26.worst_item: request_idx 94 (robovqa, 448x358 frames, 316-char question) -> measured 'Computed Tokens: 1015', 924 of them image tokens
max_input_len_headroom_2026_07_26.implication: the '<=8 frames' limit only holds for 448x252 frames (112 tok/frame). At 154 tok/frame (448x358) six frames already fill the engine; a 7th would overflow. No truncation warning appeared in the benchmark logs, and all 210 requests returned, so the published accuracies are unaffected -- but the margin was 0.9%.
max_input_len_headroom_2026_07_26.how_measured: llm_inference --engineDir engines/int4/llm --multimodalEngineDir engines/int4/visual --inputFile worst_req.json --dumpProfile (single request extracted from bench/orin_input.json)
